aircraft.engine: Rolls-Royce RB211-535 or Pratt & Whitney PW2000 series
aircraft.source: Published manufacturer/industry specifications (service ceiling, Mmo, typical cruise Mach) cross-checked across multiple independent aviation reference sites. Climb/descent table is NOT from a 757-specific published source (none was found) — it is extrapolated from SKYbrary's indicative performance data for similarly-sized narrowbody transports (737-800, A321), scaled to reflect the 757's well-documented high thrust-to-weight ratio and stronger-than-typical climb performance for its class.
aircraft.source_confidence: LIMITS (ceiling, Mmo, typical cruise Mach) are corroborated across 3+ independent sources. CLIMB/DESCENT TABLE IS AN EXTRAPOLATION, NOT A SOURCED FIGURE for this specific type — treat band-by-band deltas with more skepticism than the A321/A359/B738 files, which are anchored to published data.

climb.reference_condition: Typical airline climb profile, moderate weight, ISA. Speed schedule: 250 KIAS below FL100, ~320-330 KIAS climb, transitioning to Mach ~0.78-0.80 at crossover.
climb.notes: EXTRAPOLATED, not sourced from a 757-specific table. Built by scaling SKYbrary's published 737-800/A321 climb profiles upward by roughly 15-20% at low-to-mid altitude to reflect the 757's documented high thrust-to-weight ratio and hot-and-high capability. Treat this table as illustrative of expected shape (higher ROC at low altitude, tapering with altitude) rather than a precise reference. Weight strongly affects all of this and is unknown from ADS-B.

cruise.notes: Cruise Mach 0.80 is consistently reported across independent sources for the 757-200. Mmo is 0.86, giving the 757 an unusually large margin between typical cruise and Mmo compared to most narrowbodies.

descent.reference_condition: Typical idle-thrust descent, Mach 0.80 / ~320 KIAS / 250 KIAS below FL100
descent.notes: No 757-specific published descent table found. Figure follows the same ~3nm-per-1000ft planning rule used industry-wide for this aircraft class.
